about: Slice 11 (docs/jclass-11): Bluebonnet's textures and wear, by the texture loop (docs/texture-loop). One card per surface the plan names (steel paint, teak, varnish, bronze, duralumin, cotton sails, manila and wire rope) plus the saloon's furnishings: which of her materials it covers, the closest a camera comes, the pattern's real size, the detail maps it draws (her own, made by textures.py, or the boats' shared library), and what each of the five wear levels (Tools/texloop/levels.json) looks like on her. How much of each wear term a level gets is weathering.py's (amounts), from the loop's time and dirt numbers (Tools/texloop/wear.py); where it falls on the boat is the materials' (weathering.py dress). 'refs' are CC0 scans from Poly Haven and ambientCG whose mean albedo is a colour target for one level (the refs that share a surface, level and target are averaged, as the loop takes the photos' median); they are measured (wear_check.py), never shipped, and a surface with no fitting scan says so in 'refs_note'. Every material in the build is either in a card or in 'unweathered' with its reason: build_jclass.py stops otherwise.
salt: Galveston: she lives in salt water (Bolivar Roads), so rust weeps, verdigris and the waterline's weed and barnacles come at the salt-water rate, not the lake's third

levels.L0: launched, spring 1937: wet-look enamel, golden new teak, deep glossy varnish, new cast bronze, cream cotton, straw-gold manila, bright galvanised wire
levels.L1: her first season: the enamel's gloss a touch softer, the deck paling, rope and sails a shade greyer, bronze dulling to brown
levels.L2: six years a working yacht, half kept: enamel dull and chalky with rust weeps at the rivet lines, a silver-grey deck, varnish thin and grey at the edges, brown bronze polished where hands and rope touch, dingy sails, grey-brown rope, white zinc bloom on the wire
levels.L3: a kept classic thirty years on: everything renewed and polished, but the enamel faded, the deck scrubbed pale with its grain standing proud, the varnish deepened to dark amber, bronze bright with dark patina in the recesses, cotton yellowed a little, the wire oiled dark
levels.L4: twenty years laid up and neglected: chalked enamel with rust bleeding from every seam and chips at the sheer, weed and barnacles at the boot top, a black and green deck, varnish peeled to grey wood, verdigris on the bronze, paint flaking off the mast, mildewed sails, rotten-grey rope and rusting wire

paint.title: Steel paint
paint.what: Enamel over the riveted steel plating (slice 2's Plating relief stays): the deep blue topsides, the white boot top, the red cowl mouths, black iron; the red antifouling on the bottom and the lead; the gold-leaf cove line and lettering; the white enamel below decks
paint.closest_camera_note: the boot top from a dinghy alongside, the cabin's white paint from a berth

levels.L0: wet-look blue enamel, the plating's seams and rivets only in a raking light
levels.L1: the gloss a little softer, a faint tan scum line on the boot top
levels.L2: dull, chalky blue in blotches; thin rust weeps from rivet lines and from under the chainplates and fairleads; the boot top's weed line; the antifouling faded pink-red; the white paint below yellowing
levels.L3: polished but faded, slightly chalky blue; no rust; the boot top kept clean; the cove line's gold leaf renewed
levels.L4: heavily chalked grey-blue, rust bleeding in runs from the seams and rivet rows and from chips at the sheer; green weed along the boot top; the antifouling below chalky and crusted with barnacles; the white paint below yellow and stained with rust at the frames

teak.title: Teak deck
teak.what: The laid teak deck (slice 3's Planking: planks, king plank, covering boards and black seams), the hatch lids and the cockpit's sole; the scrubbed pine soles below decks
teak.closest_camera_note: a crew member's eye standing on deck (the helm's is 1.7 m)

levels.L0: golden-brown new teak, the black seams crisp and flush
levels.L1: the gold paling where the sun reaches it
levels.L2: silver-grey, darker in the soft grain, a few seams cracked open
levels.L3: scrubbed pale, almost white-blond, the soft grain worn down so the hard grain stands proud; seams sound
levels.L4: dark grey-black plank by plank, green algae where water lies and black mildew in the grain, open checks, failed seams standing grey and proud

varnish.title: Varnish
varnish.what: Varnished brightwork on deck (teak coamings, houses, toe rail, wheel: the 'Wood' slot) and below (the saloon's mahogany panelling and joinery, varnished pine and teak trim)
varnish.closest_camera_note: the helmsman's hands on the wheel; a sitter's eye on the saloon's panelling

levels.L0: deep, wet amber gloss over the grain
levels.L1: a slight dulling and haze on the tops of the coamings and where hands go
levels.L2: on deck the film thin and greyed at edges and tops, a few failed patches showing grey wood; below, dulled at the handholds
levels.L3: glossy again (revarnished each spring) over wood darkened to deep amber with the years
levels.L4: on deck the varnish peeled in flakes along the grain and the wood grey and black-stained under it; below, a milky bloom where damp got under the film, low down and in streaks, water rings and mildew specks

refs.note: grey wood where the finish has gone

bronze.title: Bronze
bronze.what: Cast bronze: the winches, blocks, cleats, fairleads, tracks, portlights, the binnacle and the steering gear's box, the deck fittings; the brass lamps and fittings below
bronze.closest_camera_note: a grinder's eye over a primary winch

levels.L0: new cast bronze, a golden pink sheen
levels.L2: brown patina, polished bright where hands and rope work it (the winch drums, cleat horns)
levels.L3: polished bright, as a kept classic's brightwork is, with dark, almost black patina left in the recesses
levels.L4: dark brown-black with green verdigris in the recesses and running from them, a thin green bloom on the tops

duralumin.title: Duralumin spars
duralumin.what: The riveted duralumin mast, boom and spinnaker pole and their spreaders and struts, painted pale buff (slice 4's SparPlating relief stays)
duralumin.closest_camera_note: the mast's foot from the deck

levels.L1: the gloss softening, faint grey marks where halyards slap
levels.L2: chalky flat buff, grey slap marks and grime runs under the fittings, the odd flake of paint gone
levels.L3: repainted and clean, a little yellowed
levels.L4: paint flaking off to grey duralumin round the fittings and in clusters, white corrosion powder blistering round each flake

duralumin.refs_note: Painted buff over duralumin: no CC0 scan of the period's mast paint; the blind ladder judges it.

cotton.title: Cotton sails
cotton.what: The cream Egyptian cotton sails (slice 6's cloth with its seams drawn from the UVs), the flaked and bagged sails, the bags and the cotton line; the canvas of the cots below
cotton.closest_camera_note: the genoa's tack and the main's foot from the deck

levels.L0: new cream cotton, crisp and even
levels.L1: a shade greyer, faint smudges along the foot
levels.L2: dingy grey-cream, brown grime along the foot and where the sail lies on deck, a scatter of mildew specks
levels.L3: clean, dried and stowed properly, but yellowed a little with age
levels.L4: grey with black mildew spotting along the folds it lay in, rust streaks running aft from the hanks

cotton.refs_note: No CC0 scan is undyed cream sail cotton (the linens and cottons on Poly Haven and ambientCG are dyed or modern bleached cloth), so cotton has no colour target; the blind ladder judges it.

manila.title: Manila rope
manila.what: Three-strand manila for the sheets, guys, tails, the falls of the tackles and the coils
manila.closest_camera_note: a tail on a winch's drum

levels.L0: new straw-gold manila, a little sheen, the lay crisp
levels.L1: a touch greyer, a few hairs standing off
levels.L2: grey-brown and hairy, darker where hands and the drums work it
levels.L3: kept yachts renew their running rigging every few seasons: rope a season or two old, a little grey and hairy but sound and clean
levels.L4: grey-black with green and black mildew, fuzzy, frayed

wire.title: Wire rope
wire.what: Galvanised plough-steel wire: the 1x19 standing rigging, the 7x19 runners, checkstays and halyards; the galvanised shackles, thimbles, pipe and chain, and the galley's zinc (its own kind: no iron in it to rust)
wire.closest_camera_note: a shroud's lower end at the chainplate

levels.L2: dull grey with white zinc oxide in the grooves
levels.L3: kept wire is oiled: darker, with a soft sheen
levels.L4: rust in the grooves and brown runs along the lay; the galvanised fittings rusting; the galley's zinc white and grey with oxide

furnishings.title: Furnishings below
furnishings.what: The saloon's and cabins' blue velvet, red carpet, the books' leather, the berths' linen and the porcelain basins and WCs

levels.L0: new: deep blue velvet, rich red carpet, crisp white linen
levels.L1: nearly new: the velvet's pile a little flattened on the seat fronts, the linen a shade off-white
levels.L2: the velvet's pile worn shiny on the seat fronts, the carpet worn along the gangway, the linen greyer
levels.L3: renewed, the colours a little faded by the light from the skylights
levels.L4: faded, stained, mildew on the velvet and the leather, the carpet threadbare in the gangway, the porcelain crazed and stained

furnishings.refs_note: The CC0 velvets and carpets are other colours (red velvet, beige carpet), so the furnishings have no colour target; the blind ladder judges them.

unweathered.CabinWindow: glass: the ports and skylights stay clear at every level (the game's glass draws its own film)

maps.about: Her own maps are made by textures.py into Inputs/jclass-detail (plain git, as Inputs/boat-detail); the shared ones are the boats' library (Inputs/boat-detail, Tools/boats/make_detail_textures.py), already in the game's memory for the J/22, so they cost her nothing more. Every map is box-projected in each part's own frame at its real size (tile_mm) and fades out between fade_m metres from the camera.

Gelcoat.use: the enamels' orange peel and buffing marks, the spars' paint

TeakWeathered.use: the laid deck's grain, rings and checks; the pine soles

WoodVarnish.use: the grain and pores under the varnish (deck and below)

Metal.use: bare duralumin where the paint is gone, galvanised wire and fittings

Canvas.use: the bags' and the cots' canvas

budget.about: Texture memory (the plan left it to this slice): her own maps only, since the shared library is already resident for the J/22. Block-compressed sizes with mips: BC5 normals and BC1 masks at full size on High and Ultra (the Vehicle texture groups, docs/boat-tex-medium); Medium draws no detail maps on her (colour and roughness math only, as the boats' Medium material does). Cap: 6 MB on High and Ultra, 0 on Medium.
